sourced_facts: Eqs1-2 define a normalized Gibbs binary law with unary terms and an unrestricted function of total count.
Eq4 and page4 restrict recursive cardinality subsets to nested or disjoint sets; arbitrary potentials at their counts include unary factors.
Eqs6-7 introduce deterministic sum-count auxiliary variables without changing the binary law.
§5.2 messages are exact convolutions; §5.2.3 states O(D log² D) time and O(D log D) space for balanced FFT trees, with O(D²) worst-case time for unbalanced trees.
§5.3 samples root counts then child count splits and leaves to draw exact joint configurations.
conclusion.overlap: Structured count supervision, proper count-dependent joint binary laws and exact marginal/sampling inference are established.
conclusion.proposal_adaptation: Use a visible-context conditional two-sided count potential over native NCNC residual slots and label-only TRAIN observation bits; serve structural draws through one shared nonlinear decoder.
conclusion.complexity_boundary: Arbitrary cross-side g(K_L,K_R) is not a unary potential on a single union count. It requires the separately stated full count-grid work; the paper fast bound is not claimed for that model.
